docs.text: Access PySTAC extension ¶ pystac-ext-access is a pystac Python implementation of the STAC Access Extension Specification , reads and writes STAC access metadata using the access: prefix. Describe whether data is open or restricted, what users must do to obtain it, and whether it is available immediately. Import the API from pystac.extensions.access . The implementation uses the Access v0.1.0 schema identifier . The Python package version is independent of the specification version. Why describe access? ¶ A dataset can be discoverable in a STAC catalog while still requiring registration, payment, or retrieval from an archive. The upstream Access specification makes these conditions explicit so users can understand what obtaining the data involves. Access fields on Catalogs, Collections, and Items describe the data, rather than access to the STAC metadata itself. Access conditions can differ between copies: a provider might require registration while a mirror offers a direct download. Assets and alternate assets can describe those differences. Free data that requires an account is still restricted ; price alone does not determine whether access is open . The upstream extension is currently classified as Proposal . See access concepts for the distinction between access barriers, download availability, and related STAC metadata. Start here ¶ pip install pystac-ext-access Create an Item with access metadata . Update access fields, assets, links, and Collection metadata . Look up field constraints and the Python API . Understand storage and validation . The extension supports Catalogs, Collections, Items, Assets, ItemAssetDefinitions, and Links, plus Collection summaries. It describes access conditions; it does not authenticate users, retrieve data, or enforce access control.

docs.text: Scope, architecture, and validation ¶ Access conditions and availability ¶ The upstream specification separates access barriers from availability . A dataset may require approval yet be ready to download, or be open to everyone but need retrieval first. Availability describes the client's workflow, rather than the storage technology: Value What the client needs to do online Download the data directly. nearline Request the download and wait while that request triggers retrieval; no separate order is needed. offline Explicitly initiate retrieval, for example through an order, before downloading. access:retrieval_time estimates the wait for nearline or offline data. The specification says to ignore it for online data. How Access fits with other STAC metadata ¶ The upstream guidance distinguishes several responsibilities: Access describes eligibility, barriers, instructions, and availability. Authentication describes the technical authentication process, such as token endpoints and OAuth flows. Order describes a transaction, such as retrieving an offline product. License describes permitted uses of the data after access is obtained; it does not replace access conditions. For example, registration instructions belong in Access metadata, while the protocol for obtaining a token belongs in the Authentication extension. Links can direct users to registration, access-request, payment, or terms-of-service pages using the specification's relation types . Package structure ¶ The distribution is named pystac-ext-access , while the import path is pystac.extensions.access . The package shares PySTAC's extension namespace. AccessExtension.ext() wraps a Catalog, Collection, Item, Asset, ItemAssetDefinition, or Link. AccessExtension.summaries() wraps Collection summaries. These wrappers update the original objects, which serialize through PySTAC's normal to_dict() method. Metadata storage ¶ Object Storage Item properties Catalog or Collection extra_fields , serialized at the top level Asset or Link extra_fields ItemAssetDefinition properties Collection summaries summaries Assets belonging to an Item fall back to the Item's properties when an access field is missing locally. Setters and removal operations change only the asset. Other wrappers do not inherit access fields from their owners or parent catalogs. Nested Alternate and AssetFields values preserve JSON members and provide live wrappers over stored dictionaries. They do not resolve URLs or expand templates. Validation boundaries ¶ The wrapper checks supported targets and field names. Type annotations help callers choose values, but setters do not enforce the complete schema. Neither apply() nor to_dict() validates the resulting STAC document. apply() checks names and target compatibility first, then assigns fields; it is not a transactional validation API. For full STAC and extension validation, install PySTAC's validation extra: python -m pip install "pystac[validation]>=1,<2" Then call item.validate() or collection.validate() on a complete STAC object. Validation can retrieve remote schemas, so their URLs must be reachable or supplied through an application-configured validator. For explicit jsonschema validation, enable a FormatChecker with duration support to check access:retrieval_time . The repository's schema integrity tests run offline against tests/data/access-schema.json , copied from the upstream main branch. They check Draft 7 schema validity, the extension identifier, valid and invalid field values, nested locations, summaries, and extension serialization. They validate the Access contract alone, rather than the full STAC core schema, and do not detect later upstream changes until the snapshot is refreshed. Schema versions and generated code ¶ The extension registers https://stac-extensions.github.io/access/v0.1.0/schema.json . has_extension() checks for that exact identifier. The module provides no migration hooks for older or alternative identifiers. The Python implementation is generated. Schema-derived changes belong in the authoritative schema and generation workflow; generated classes should not be edited by hand. The field reference documents the currently generated API, including target restrictions and camelCase template properties. Access metadata describes availability and conditions of access. Authentication, authorization, payments, and data retrieval remain the responsibility of the application and data provider.

docs.text: Work with access metadata ¶ The first examples continue from the Item created in the tutorial . Update or remove fields ¶ access = AccessExtension . ext ( item ) access . apply ( availability = "online" , retrieval_time = None ) assert access . type == "restricted" assert "access:retrieval_time" not in item . properties access . instructions = "Register, then download the dataset." access . clear ( "instructions" ) assert "access:instructions" not in item . properties ext(item) requires the extension to be declared already. Use add_if_missing=True when first attaching it. apply() changes only supplied fields; assigning None removes a field. clear() takes the Python property name, such as retrieval_time , rather than the STAC field name. Removing restrictions while keeping type="restricted" produces invalid metadata. Setters do not enforce this relationship; validate the resulting document. Read and override asset fields ¶ asset = pystac . Asset ( href = "https://example.org/data.tif" , media_type = "image/tiff" ) item . add_asset ( "data" , asset ) asset_access = AccessExtension . ext ( asset ) assert asset_access . availability == "online" asset_access . availability = "offline" assert asset . extra_fields [ "access:availability" ] == "offline" assert access . availability == "online" asset_access . availability = None assert asset_access . availability == "online" Attach an asset to its owner before wrapping it. An Item asset reads missing fields from the Item's properties; writes affect the asset only. Removing an override exposes the Item value again. Collection assets have no corresponding fallback. Describe alternate access ¶ from pystac.extensions.access import Alternate asset_access . alternate = { "mirror" : Alternate . from_dict ({ "href" : "https://mirror.example.org/data.tif" , "access:type" : "open" , "access:availability" : "online" , }) } assert asset . extra_fields [ "alternate" ][ "mirror" ][ "access:type" ] == "open" Alternate.create() builds typed access fields. from_dict() also preserves other members such as href . Describing an alternate does not download it. Extend a Collection and its item asset definitions ¶ This example is independent of the Item above: import pystac from pystac.extensions.access import AccessExtension collection = pystac . Collection ( id = "example-collection" , description = "Example collection with registration requirements" , extent = pystac . Extent ( spatial = pystac . SpatialExtent ([[ - 180 , - 90 , 180 , 90 ]]), temporal = pystac . TemporalExtent ([[ None , None ]]), ), ) collection_access = AccessExtension . ext ( collection , add_if_missing = True ) collection_access . apply ( type = "restricted" , restrictions = [ "registration" ]) collection . item_assets = { "data" : pystac . ItemAssetDefinition ({ "type" : "image/tiff" , "roles" : [ "data" ]}) } definition = collection . item_assets [ "data" ] definition_access = AccessExtension . ext ( definition ) definition_access . availability = "nearline" Catalogs use the same AccessExtension.ext(catalog, add_if_missing=True) entry point. Catalog and Collection access fields are stored at the top level of their serialized documents. Describe links and templates ¶ Continue with the Collection above: from pystac.extensions.access import Alternate , AssetFields link = pystac . Link ( rel = "enclosure" , target = "https://example.org/download" ) collection . add_link ( link ) AccessExtension . ext ( link ) . apply ( type = "restricted" , restrictions = [ "agreement" ]) collection_access . assetTemplates = { "data" : AssetFields . create ( availability = "nearline" , retrieval_time = "PT1H" ) } collection_access . linkTemplates = [ Alternate . create ( type = "open" )] Attach a Link to an owner before extending it. assetTemplates and linkTemplates retain their schema-defined camelCase names in the Python API and are supported on Catalogs and Collections. These helpers store metadata; they do not expand templates into assets or links. Set Collection summaries ¶ summaries = AccessExtension . summaries ( collection ) summaries . type = [ "open" , "restricted" ] summaries . availability = [ "online" , "nearline" ] summaries . retrieval_time = pystac . RangeSummary ( "PT1H" , "P1D" ) assert collection . summaries . to_dict ()[ "access:retrieval_time" ] == { "minimum" : "PT1H" , "maximum" : "P1D" } Summaries describe values across the Collection. They are separate from the Collection's own access fields. Set a summary property to None to remove it. See the field reference for supported representations.

docs.text: Access fields ¶ The implementation targets the Access v0.1.0 schema . The repository tests preserve an upstream schema snapshot in tests/data/access-schema.json . Common fields ¶ These fields apply to Catalogs, Collections, Items, Assets, ItemAssetDefinitions, and Links. STAC field Python property Schema constraint access:type type open , embargoed , restricted , or closed . access:restrictions restrictions Non-empty list of unique values: registration , agreement , data_fee , transfer_fee , membership , or approval . access:instructions instructions Non-empty string explaining how to obtain access. access:availability availability online , nearline , or offline . access:retrieval_time retrieval_time ISO 8601 duration string, for example PT1H or P1D . Requires format checking during validation. All common fields are optional except that access:type="restricted" requires access:restrictions . The schema rejects unknown access: fields but permits other namespaces. The extension inserts no default field values. These are schema constraints, not setter checks. Python annotations describe accepted types, but setters do not enforce enums, duration syntax, or cross-field requirements at runtime. Nested structures ¶ STAC field and Python property Python value Supported wrapper targets alternate dict[str, Alternate] Asset, ItemAssetDefinition assetTemplates dict[str, AssetFields] Catalog, Collection linkTemplates list[Alternate] Catalog, Collection Alternate wraps the common access fields. AssetFields wraps the common fields plus alternate . Both support create() , from_dict() , to_dict() , apply() , clear() , and set_null() . from_dict() wraps its input by reference by default; pass copy=True for an independent deep copy. to_dict() returns the live backing dictionary. Unknown members are preserved, with their validity determined by the schema. Nested objects read through extension getters also wrap the stored dictionaries. Updates, missing values, and null ¶ Getters return None for absent fields, subject to Item asset fallback. Setting a property to None removes it. apply() preserves omitted fields and removes fields explicitly passed as None . Unknown or inapplicable field names are rejected before an extension apply() begins assigning values. clear("retrieval_time") removes the stored field. set_null("retrieval_time") writes explicit JSON null instead. The common Access field schemas do not permit null, so this low-level operation produces metadata that fails schema validation. Collection summaries ¶ AccessExtension.summaries(collection, add_if_missing=True) exposes the five common fields as summary properties. Summary arrays contain the corresponding field values; restrictions contains individual restriction strings rather than lists of strings. The schema also allows object summaries. Retrieval-time objects validate minimum and maximum as duration strings. The summary wrapper reads objects containing both bounds as pystac.RangeSummary and preserves other object summaries as dictionaries. See working examples and the Python API .

docs.text: Create an Item with access metadata ¶ Install the package using the installation guide . This example describes an imaginary dataset that requires registration and takes an hour to retrieve. Create and extend an Item ¶ from datetime import datetime , timezone import pystac from pystac.extensions.access import AccessExtension item = pystac . Item ( id = "example-access" , geometry = None , bbox = None , datetime = datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 , tzinfo = timezone . utc ), properties = { "title" : "Example dataset" }, ) access = AccessExtension . ext ( item , add_if_missing = True ) access . apply ( type = "restricted" , restrictions = [ "registration" ], availability = "nearline" , retrieval_time = "PT1H" , instructions = "Register with the provider before requesting this dataset." , ) assert access . type == "restricted" assert item . properties [ "access:retrieval_time" ] == "PT1H" assert AccessExtension . get_schema_uri () in item . stac_extensions add_if_missing=True registers the extension on the Item. The wrapper mutates the Item in place. retrieval_time is an ISO 8601 duration string; PT1H means one hour. The schema requires a non-empty restrictions list when access:type is restricted . Serialize and read back ¶ Continue in the same Python session: import json payload = item . to_dict () print ( json . dumps ( payload , indent = 2 )) restored_item = pystac . Item . from_dict ( payload ) restored = AccessExtension . ext ( restored_item ) assert restored . restrictions == [ "registration" ] assert restored . retrieval_time == "PT1H" Serialization does not perform JSON Schema validation. See validation boundaries before exporting documents. Continue with the how-to guide to update fields and describe access to individual assets. apply() preserves fields whose arguments are omitted.
